notes.text: Prepared detailed plan at 1d533f7c3f6c44993044bb498067d609f7ea2545; see NOTE-20260908-compact-mcp-status-plan. One MCP transport/serialization probe passed (577 ms overall) with synthetic small/populated fixtures: full project status 2,519/70,681 UTF-8 text bytes, single test 760/4,282 bytes, project list 489 bytes in both. Found remaining full-query costs, raw session owner exposure in legacy projections, and incomplete/noisy dashboard event coverage for waiting. Plan proposes additive compact APIs, safe projections and bounded shared polling, with source-attribution coordination. No compact feature, real claim/test workflow benchmark, token measurement or deployment performed; item remains open, priority next.

problem: Project status snapshots include logs, worktree metadata, test presets/history, and storage data even when an agent only needs placement, owner, phase, and available capacity. Repeated polling spends context and tool calls on unchanged details.

After the dashboard fix, list_projects no longer discovers Git, but detailed projectSnapshot still forces fresh metadata and get_test_run reads/parses retained logs. Filtering those fields only after assembly would leave avoidable work on the compact path.
Existing reservation owner strings embed raw MCP session IDs. Dashboard SSE is noisy on logs and does not cover every MCP-only reservation change, so it is not a complete wait-for-status signal.

risk.rollback: Revert the focused implementation change without changing existing project configuration or unrelated runtime ownership.

scope: Add a compatible compact status contract containing stable project/run identifiers, exact worktree path, runtime phase, safe owner label, capacity, error code, and state revision/timestamp.
Make logs, storage history, test history, and preset details explicit bounded reads or opt-in expansions. Preserve existing clients through additive options or separately named tools.
Offer bounded wait-for-change or actionable retry-after information for status polling. Document a short inspect -> act -> wait -> verify -> release workflow in the portable skill.
Keep raw credentials, lease secrets, session identifiers, and environment values out of the compact contract. Avoid automatic release, restart, or force claim.

Read notes/NOTE-20260908-compact-mcp-status-plan/implementation-plan.md before implementation. It defines proposed tool fields, explicit detail reads, limits, compatible mutation output modes and the delivery sequence.

Add narrow runtime, effective-reservation and projected test-run queries without Git, preset/storage work, runtime-history copying or logs_json decoding. Preserve one lifecycle/capacity authority and one SQLite owner.

Implement bounded shared sampling only while waiters exist: proposed one-second interval, 10-second default/20-second maximum wait, 128 global waiters, four per session and 64 distinct targets. Compare opaque state cursors excluding logs and sampling timestamps; return only changed snapshots or a small timeout result.

Preserve source qualification and queued versus observed execution HEAD from the actual source-attribution contract, or explicit legacy uncertainty. Do not convert a compact passed phase into an unsupported verified-commit claim.

Add optional compact claim/enqueue response modes with full defaults unchanged. Keep accepted handles and leaseHeld on failure, all idempotency/authorization behavior, and independent claim renewal; cancellation of a wait never mutates runtime, claims or tests.

Update the repository portable skill only with implemented tool names, capability fallback and inspect/act/wait/verify/release guidance. Keep all proposed APIs and defaults clearly marked until shipped.
source: Repository assessment and owner direction on 2026-09-05
title: Offer compact MCP status and fetch details only when needed
validation: Compare response bytes and tool-call counts for the same successful claim and queued-test workflows before and after. Keep the actual work and evidence identical; report token estimates only with a named tokenizer.
Verify a quiet status response omits bulky logs/history, requested details stay bounded, and existing clients retain their supported behavior.
Verify wait timeout, disconnect, state change, authorization failure, and cancellation cannot retain an unbounded waiter or silently repeat a mutation.

Use the attached small/populated baseline fixture and add actual compact measurements. Baseline get_project_status text payload was 2,519/70,681 bytes and get_test_run was 760/4,282 bytes. These are UTF-8 MCP payloads with stubbed application data, not tokens, production performance or workflow savings.

Assert zero Git, preset discovery, storage scheduling, full snapshots and log/history decoding for compact reads/waits. Growing log/history data must not inflate compact payloads; bound output without truncating operation identifiers or worktree paths.

Test same-target poll sharing, idle teardown, meaningful cursor changes, quiet lease expiry, MCP-only changes, registration races, timeout, disconnect/session expiry/cancellation, retention/removal, query errors and waiter saturation.

Assert raw session IDs, tokens, environment values, free-form owner/reason data and technical error secrets never appear in compact output. Verify legacy tools/resources/default mutation schemas and source-attribution semantics remain supported.

Run focused query/wait/MCP/SQLite tests, pnpm check and pnpm build; verify affected dashboard flows if shared changes alter UI behavior. Measure all calls and required detail evidence in fixed claim and queued-test workflows before claiming savings.
value: Routine agent work uses fewer tokens and repeated tool calls while keeping enough evidence to act correctly.
